root_cause.text: The sps30_i2c_read_meas() function incorrectly calculates the buffer size by using sizeof(num) (which evaluates to sizeof(size_t), 8 bytes on 64-bit systems) instead of sizeof(*meas) (which is sizeof(__be32), 4 bytes), causing an oversized buffer allocation that does not match the actual data element type being read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `sizeof(num) * num` to `sizeof(*meas) * num` in the sps30_i2c_command() call. The variable `num` is of type `size_t`, so `sizeof(num)` returns 8 bytes on 64-bit architectures, whereas the buffer `meas` is declared as `__be32 *meas` (4-byte elements). The fix uses `sizeof(*meas)` to correctly dereference the pointer type and match the intended 4-byte element size for the I2C read operation.
